plan.title: fix(scope): completed/ accepts an unguarded write and there is no way to restamp it

narratives.Description: fix(scope): completed/ accepts an unguarded write and there is no way to restamp it
narratives.Overview:
> Recut after a three-critic panel refuted the original framing. The gate is **not** broken — presence-only is the #3264 / #3476 question, answered correctly. The provenance boundary split to #3686. What remains is the route around the completion verb and the fact that there is no way back once someone takes it. Prior body and full critique record are in this issue's history and comments.

## What happened

#3660 merged as PR #3677, squash `269a07e5`. That commit contains both the product change and `xbrief/completed/2026-08-24-3660-…xbrief.json`, an artifact with no `completionProvenance`, no `mergeCommit`, no `disposition`.

The feature-branch history shows how, and it is not what this issue originally claimed:

| Commit | Time | Change | Stated reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00c09ddf` | 23:06:11 | **adds** `xbrief/active/…3660….json` beside the product diff | — |
| `5a9a193e` | 23:09:14 | **deletes** it | `verify:scope-provenance` fails when an active xBRIEF with `file_scope` lands in the same PR as product files and no merge-base digest exists; minting one needs a human TTY |
| `d0e535a2` | 23:09:55 | **adds** the same basename under `completed/` | place the completed brief in the work PR so completed-tracked does not need a leftover chore after merge |

Forty-one seconds between the block and the workaround. The land gate then ran after merge, saw a terminal blob on the tip, and exited 0 — which is its designed green path.

## Defect 1: `completed/` accepts an unguarded write

Every in-process writer that lands in `completed/` goes through the transition verb:

| Path | Source folder | Stamps provenance |
|---|---|---|
| `runTransition("complete")` | `active/` only | yes, when code-bearing and the delivery gate returns provenance |
| `runTransition("fail")` | `active/` only | no — the delivery gate runs only for `complete` |
| `swarm:complete-cohort` / `finalize-cohort` | wraps `complete` | same as complete |

There is no other in-process writer. But `completed/` is an ordinary directory, no hook guards it, and `git add` works. That is what happened.

This is boundary-independent. Whatever the artifact eventually contains — see #3686 — a filesystem write that bypasses the transition verb should not be able to land there.

## Defect 2: there is no way back, and the code written for it is dead

Once a husk is in `completed/`, no verb can restamp it.

`complete` allows only `active/` as a source (`scope/constants.ts:32`), so it refuses with *requires file in active/. File is in completed/.*

The already-completed no-op that would handle this is unreachable. `transition.ts:175` reads `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS[act]` and only enters the block when it is defined — but `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` (`constants.ts:45-48`) contains only `block` and `unblock`. So for `complete`, `requiredStatus` is `undefined` and the whole branch is skipped, **including the code written under #3041 specifically for `act === "complete" && currentFolder === "completed"` to surface the stored delivery disposition.**

That branch has never executed. It was written for exactly this recovery case.

These two defects ship together. Closing the route without a recovery path traps the next worker who hits the scope-provenance blocker: unable to co-land, unable to restamp afterwards.

## Fix

- Refuse a newly added `completed/` blob that was not written by `runTransition`. Historical corpus advisory, new work hard — the split `doctor/checks.ts` already uses for pre-#2862 open items.
- Lift the already-completed handling out of the `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` guard so it actually runs for `complete`, and teach it to stamp a file already in `completed/` rather than only print the disposition.
- Fix the worker-facing text. After a provenance-gated product PR strips `active/` from the change set, the designed remainder is a leftover land PR (#3476). The remediation should say that, because routing around the verb is currently the path of least resistance and nothing tells the worker otherwise.

## Explicitly not in scope

**Do not widen `verify:completed-tracked`.** It answers the #3264 / #3476 land question — is a tracked terminal artifact on the delivery tip — and presence-only is that question answered correctly. Making it a stamp-quality detector is a new gate, not a repair. The original body claimed this gate "exists to catch exactly this"; that is false as a reading of either issue and is withdrawn.

**Do not require provenance in the artifact.** That is #3686. A blanket requirement would break compliant non-code-bearing completes (where `evaluateDeliveryGate` legitimately returns null provenance) and `scope:fail` (which stamps nothing by design), and it would red the 1122 pre-gate artifacts.

**Do not merge with #3675.** Different verbs, different times — stamp quality inside a gate that ran, versus a land gate that never asked. #3675 must be bound before any stamp-quality gate exists, or `--merge-commit origin/master` becomes the way back to green.

## Scale, honestly

Post-gate compliance is 88.4% — 168 of 190 completed artifacts since 2026-08-02, against 1 of 1122 before. #3660 is the only work-PR co-land bypass; two chore PRs merely forgot the stamp.

The original body argued the incentive runs backwards and this would recur. That claim is bounded to *this can happen*, not *this is happening*. The route is worth closing because it is unguarded, not because it is being used.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A `completed/` blob added without `runTransition` is refused on new work
- [ ] Pre-existing artifacts are advisory, not red
- [ ] `scope:complete` can stamp a brief already in `completed/`, so recovery does not require a folder round-trip
- [ ] The #3041 disposition branch actually executes for `complete`
- [ ] Remediation text names the leftover land PR as the designed path after a scope-provenance strip
- [ ] `verify:completed-tracked` is unchanged
- [ ] Non-code-bearing and `failed` completions pass unchanged
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line

## Critique record

Critics: [A](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3679#issuecomment-5397908858), [B](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3679#issuecomment-5397881177), [C](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3679#issuecomment-5398022686). ## Disclosure

I filed this issue. I also filed its parent #3674, drove that arc, and filed #3675, #3678 and #3680 out of the same investigation. This is a self-authored issue inside a self-authored family, and the family has a shape I chose.

**I have a specific conflict of interest a critic should press on.**

#3678 is being built right now. It makes lifecycle PRs cheaper by skipping non-required CI jobs on artifact-only diffs. Its entire value depends on lifecycle PRs continuing to exist.

If this issue concludes that completion provenance should *not* live in the committed artifact — that the right fix is to eliminate the second PR rather than enforce the record it carries — then #3678 is work I commissioned that partly did not need doing, and #3680 is a child I filed that partly should not exist.

I have an incentive to frame "enforce provenance" as the obvious answer and to treat "stop requiring it" as out of scope. **Test that.** The scope section of this body does exactly that framing, and I wrote it before the #3631 panel produced the argument against it.

**A third arc has already pointed here.** All three critics on #3631 independently recommended sequencing this issue ahead of cheapening work, and one argued directly that eliminating lifecycle PRs beats optimizing them because it removes the highest-volume chore class. That argument was made without seeing this issue.

## Confidence

**Measured, and I verified these myself at `269a07e5` — a critic should nonetheless re-verify, because I am the author and these are the claims the issue rests on:**

`evaluateCompletedTracked` and the CLI wrapper contain no reference to `completionProvenance`, `disposition`, or `mergeCommit`. The check is presence-on-delivery-tip only.

The #3660 completed artifact has top-level keys `xBRIEFInfo`, `plan`, `vBRIEFInfo` and carries none of those fields.

`verify:completed-tracked --issue 3660` exited 0.

#3657 and #3651 landed via separate chore commits carrying `completionProvenance` and `disposition: delivered`; #3660 co-landed in its work PR carrying neither.

**Asserted, and not verified:**

That the worker's reported blocker — `scope:complete` refusing a non-`active/` path — is the actual mechanism by which the brief reached `completed/`. I have the worker's report and the resulting artifact. I did not reproduce the failure.

That this recurs rather than being a one-off. One instance is one instance. The incentive argument is inference, not measurement.

That the gate "exists to catch exactly this." That is my characterization of #3476's intent, not a quote from its design.

```
audit:presence-only sha=269a07e5 pointer=packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:450-470 reading=measured
audit:artifact-no-provenance sha=269a07e5 pointer=xbrief/completed/2026-08-24-3660-fixdesign-critique-panel-ceiling-and-dual-stop-accounting.xbrief.json:1-1 reading=measured

audit:gate-intent sha=269a07e5 pointer=comment:none reading=asserted
```

The first two arrived from #3674 unaudited because they postdated that arc's input ceiling. They are in envelope here.

## Refutation target

> **The fix is to make completion provenance mandatory in the committed artifact and have `verify:completed-tracked` enforce it.**

This is the direction my scope section assumes. It is the load-bearing claim because everything else follows from it: if provenance must live in the artifact, and the delivery-ancestry gate makes stamping it impossible before the merge commit exists, then a second PR is structurally required forever — and #3678 and #3680 become permanent infrastructure rather than a transitional cost.

The opposing position, which a critic should take seriously: the artifact is the wrong home for delivery provenance. The information is derivable from the forge — which PR merged, when, at what SHA — and committing a hand-stamped copy of it creates a write that must happen after the fact, which is precisely what forces the second PR. On that reading the fix is to stop requiring the artifact to assert it, and the gate should check something the worker can satisfy before merge.

I do not know which is right. I filed the issue assuming the first.

## Notes for critics

**Read #3674's arc before this one.** Its central finding is that the delivery-ancestry gate, introduced 2026-08-02, requires the merge commit to be an ancestor of the remote delivery ref, which makes co-landing a `delivered` completion structurally impossible. That finding is why this issue exists and it constrains every fix.

**Two adjacent issues are deliberately not this one.** #3675 is the gate accepting an unbound merge commit — a weak check inside a gate that ran. This is a gate that never ran, with no backstop noticing. If you conclude they should merge, say so.

**Watch for gate-integrity adjacency (#3156).** Any resolution that makes the gate pass more easily needs to be distinguishable from weakening a gate to go green.

**The incentive claim is the weakest thing here** and I would rather it be attacked than accepted. It rests on one instance and on my reading of what a worker will do under cost pressure.

## Stop 2 — variant selection

**Charter:** refutation. The write-back marks the target: *the fix is to make completion provenance mandatory in the committed artifact and have `verify:completed-tracked` enforce it.*

**Spend:** N=3.

**Why the panel.** Both permission conditions hold. The solution space is genuinely open in a way the body conceals — it assumes enforcement and never considers that the artifact may be the wrong home for the record. Blast radius is high: this is the lifecycle gate every story passes through, the issue carries a `security` label, and the answer determines whether a whole PR class is permanent infrastructure or a transitional cost. Two builds are in flight whose value depends on that answer.

This issue is also the sequencing keystone. Three critics on #3631 independently put it ahead of cheapening work; #3680 is gated on it. Getting it wrong is expensive in both directions — enforcing a record nobody needs, or dropping a record that turns out to be load-bearing for audit.

## Routing

Three decorrelated angles, three models. Each sibling gets the charter; none may read another's post.

**A — where provenance belongs.** Is the committed artifact the right home? What is derivable from the forge, what is not, and what would be lost by deriving rather than stamping? Does the delivery-ancestry gate leave any pre-merge-satisfiable formulation?

**B — the gate and its integrity.** Is presence-only actually wrong, or correct for the question #3476 asks? What should the backstop check, and what closes the route by which a brief reaches `completed/` without the verb? Distinguish a legitimate gate change from weakening a gate to go green.

**C — recurrence and incentive.** Is the incentive claim true? Measure it. Is #3660 a one-off caused by a specific blocker, or the first instance of a pattern? What does the actual completed corpus show about provenance coverage over time, and does the compliant path really cost more?

## Accounting

An N=3 panel is permitted three round-1 posts and no default retry. A fourth requires the operator to raise the cap for this arc, recorded.

The parent authored this issue, its parent, and three of its siblings, and has a disclosed interest in one outcome. Disclosure is in the write-back. ## Steelman of the position I am rejecting

A completed xBRIEF is the durable audit object. If the only DONE backstop asks “is a file on the delivery tip?”, a worker can mint a husk with `plan.status: completed` and every later reader treats the story as closed-with-evidence. `scope:complete` already knows how to stamp provenance, including explicit non-delivery. The cheapest durable repair is to make the backstop require that stamp. Closing the `git mv` route without a backstop still fails when someone writes the file by hand. Historical corpus is a migration, not a reason to leave the hole.

That steelman is why the author’s scope section treats enforcement as obvious. It is also the reading that keeps leftover lifecycle PRs structurally required, which is the disclosed interest.

## Findings

### F1. Presence-only is the question #3476 built — `blocks-the-design`

`verify:completed-tracked` was not built to catch zero delivery evidence. #3264’s v1 rule: if a scoped GitHub issue is closed, the delivery-branch tip must contain a **tracked** `completed/` or `cancelled/` artifact that references it. #3476 added `--issue N` against `origin/<deliveryBranch>` so drive-to DONE cannot green-skip laptop residue. Proposed item 2 was **`scope:complete` stay fs-only**. Proposed item 4 was **keep this verb off `task check`**.

The executable design is the test file, not the author’s characterization. `completed-tracked-on-delivery.test.ts` asserts missing land, feature-HEAD-only land, and `--issue` scoping. It never reads blob contents beyond issue refs. `classifyStoredDeliveryDisposition` (`delivery-evidence.ts:188-201`) already treats a missing stamp as `unknown` / `unverified`, not `delivered`. A husk does not assert delivery. It asserts folder presence. That is the #3476 question, answered correctly.

A gate that correctly answers a narrow question is not broken because a wider question exists. The author’s “the gate exists to catch exactly this” (`audit:gate-intent`, marked asserted) is false as a reading of #3476 / #3264. Widening this verb to stamp-quality is a **new gate**, not a repair of a broken one. Naming it as a fix to `verify:completed-tracked` smuggles a standard change through a recurrence filing.

At `269a07e5`, `git grep -l completionProvenance` hits **169** of **1312** `xbrief/completed/` blobs. Zero `deliveryProvenance`. A mandatory-stamp check with no grandfather reds about 87% of the corpus. The in-tree pattern for this class is already written: `checkCompletedOpenItems` (`doctor/checks.ts:1331-1333`) is advisory on historical pre-#2862 corpora; `scope:complete` fails closed on new work. The proposal does not name that migration. Silence here is a corpus-red design.

### F2. Enforcing the stamp and closing the route are two fixes; only the route prevents recurrence — `blocks-the-design`

Every production writer that lands in `completed/` through the verb:

| Path | Source folder | Stamps provenance? |
|---|---|---|
| `runTransition("complete")` / `scope:complete` | `active/` only (`constants.ts:32`) | yes, if code-bearing and the delivery gate returns provenance |
| `runTransition("fail")` / `scope:fail` | `active/` only (`constants.ts:33`) | **no** — delivery gate runs only for `act === "complete"` (`transition.ts:252`) |
| `swarm:complete-cohort` / `swarm:finalize-cohort` | wraps `runTransition("complete")` | same as complete |

There is no other in-process writer. `completed/` is an ordinary directory. No hook under `.githooks` mentions it. A worker can `git add` a new file there. That is what happened.

PR #3677 file status for the artifact is `added`, not `renamed`. Feature-branch history at the same SHA family:

1. `00c09ddf` — added `xbrief/active/2026-08-24-3660-…xbrief.json` next to the product diff.
2. `5a9a193e` (three minutes later) — **deleted** that active file. Message: `verify:scope-provenance` fails when an active xBRIEF with `file_scope` lands in the same PR as product files and no merge-base digest exists; mint needs a human TTY; keep the brief local for post-merge complete.
3. `d0e535a2` (41 seconds after that) — **added** the same basename under `completed/`. Message: place the completed brief in the work PR so completed-tracked does not need a leftover chore after merge.

The backstop did not fail to run. It ran after merge, saw a terminal blob on the tip, and exited 0. That is the designed green path for land. Recurrence is prevented by refusing an unguarded write into `completed/`, or by making the verb the only writer — not by asking the land detector a stamp-quality question after the write already shipped.

### F3. Mandatory provenance in this backstop fights the verb that already exists — `blocks-the-design`

Three collisions, all in the current complete path:

1. **Non-code-bearing.** `evaluateDeliveryGate` (`delivery-evidence.ts:341-347`) returns `ok: true` with `provenance: null` for non-code-bearing scopes. `transition.ts:266-274` stamps only when `gate.provenance !== null`. A blanket “artifact must carry `completionProvenance`” makes the **compliant** docs/process complete fail DONE. The issue named non-delivery dispositions as the exception; those **do** stamp. The path that stamps nothing is non-code-bearing, and `fail`.
2. **No recovery once the file is in `completed/`.** `complete` allows only `active/` (`constants.ts:32`; refuse at `transition.ts:151-159`: `requires file in active/. File is in completed/.`). The no-op at `:177-187` for already-completed never runs: `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` has no `complete` entry, so `requiredStatus` is undefined. After a husk lands, the worker cannot restamp with the verb. The proposed backstop would go red with no verb remediation. That is a new trap, not a tighter gate.
3. **#3675 becomes the compliance path.** `verifyDeliveryAncestry` is reachability (`gitIsAncestor`, same SHA counts, `git.ts:72-80`). `main.ts:224` synthesizes `mergedAt: "supplied"` whenever `--merge-commit` is passed. A worker who must produce a stamp before their own merge exists can feed `origin/master`. If this issue requires the stamp and #3675 is still open, the unbound-ancestor hole is how green is restored. That is routing around a stronger backstop through a weaker verb — the #3156 class this filing asked us to watch.

Do not merge #3679 and #3675. Different verbs, different times (stamp quality inside a gate that ran vs a land gate that never asked stamp quality). Sequence them: do not require a stamp in `completed-tracked` until the stamp is bound to the story.

### F4. The worker-facing failure is real, and it is not the one asserted — `sharpens-framing`

`audit:blocker-mechanism` was marked asserted. The folder check is real in code: `scope:complete` on a `completed/` path refuses. The incident commits do not show that refuse as the reason.

They show `verify:scope-provenance` blocking an **active** brief in a product PR (`evaluate.ts:391-409`, `active-xbrief-modified-without-digest`; human mint required for non-empty `file_scope`). The worker dropped `active/` from the change set and, 41 seconds later, wrote `completed/` so the leftover chore would not be needed. The local active copy was explicitly kept for post-merge complete, then bypassed.

Two verb holes still matter, and they are not “no `active/` path”:

- **Delivery ancestry (#3041 / #3674).** A code-bearing `delivered` complete cannot run until the merge commit is an ancestor of refreshed `origin/<deliveryBranch>`. Co-landing a honest `delivered` stamp in the work PR is structurally impossible. That is #3674’s title, not a missing folder.
- **Scope-provenance vs product diff.** Shipping `active/` + `file_scope` + product files in one PR fails without a human TTY mint. That is what removed the committed `active/` path.

The usability hole worth fixing is: after provenance-gated product PRs strip `active/` from the change set, the designed remainder is a leftover land PR (#3476). The worker-facing text should say that, and `scope:complete` should be able to stamp a file already in `completed/` so recovery does not require a folder round-trip. That is secondary to closing the unguarded write. It is not a reason to change the land detector’s question.

### F5. Gate integrity (#3156): this incident was a route-around, not a weakened gate — `sharpens-framing`

Three-way split, as asked:

| Class | This incident | Proposed “enforce provenance in `completed-tracked`” |
|---|---|---|
| Gate legitimately not applying | `verify:completed-tracked` applied its land question and passed. `scope:complete` never ran, so the delivery gate did not apply. | Widening the land verb is a named standard change. Allowed only as itself, with grandfather, not as a silent sibling of a recurrence fix. |
| Gate routed around | Yes. Filesystem add under `completed/` skipped `runTransition`. `d0e535a2` states the motive: skip the leftover chore. | A stamp requirement without #3675 bind routes workers into `--merge-commit origin/master`. |
| Gate weakened to go green | No. Nothing in the evaluator was edited. `scope-provenance` was not weakened; the triggering `active/` file was removed. | A broad grandfather that leaves presence-only green is a weaken. An ungrandfathered corpus-red will pressure that weaken. |

#3156 forbids clearing red by editing the failing evaluator. This filing is the opposite temptation: edit a **green** evaluator so a different failure becomes visible. That can be legitimate. It is still a gate-definition change. It is not how you close a route.

### F6. Press on the disclosed conflict — `sharpens-framing`

The author asked to be pressed. The scope section decides “require the stamp, then have this backstop enforce it” before the critique. That pairing is the only pairing that makes leftover lifecycle PRs permanent infrastructure: delivery ancestry forbids an honest pre-merge `delivered` stamp, so the stamp must be a second write, so #3678 (cheapen those PRs) and #3680 stay load-bearing.

The opposing position the write-back offered — derive delivery from the forge, stop requiring the artifact to assert it — is the one that makes #3678 partly unnecessary. The author’s “I do not know which is right” sits under a scope that only operationalizes the first. Sibling A owns where the record belongs. From this gate: **do not put that unresolved ownership decision into `verify:completed-tracked`**. This verb answers land. Stamp ownership is a different surface. Choosing the surface that preserves the second PR, while #3678 is in flight, is the conflict operating.

`d0e535a2` is one instance of leftover-chore avoidance, not a recurrence series. I am not claiming the incentive generalizes. I am claiming the proposed fix is the one the conflict prefers, and the gate does not need it.

### F7. `fail` and the dead complete-on-completed no-op — `footnote`

`scope:fail` lands in `completed/` with `plan.status: failed` and no provenance stamp. A mandatory-stamp backstop that does not carve `failed` reds a documented terminal status (`completed-consistency.ts` / D2/D13).

The complete-on-completed no-op in `transition.ts:177-187` is dead. Anyone who believes “complete is idempotent on `completed/`” will hit the folder refuse instead. If recovery after a husk is in scope, that no-op has to be lifted out of `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` and taught to stamp, not merely print `deliveryDisposition`.

## Road not taken

Keep `verify:completed-tracked` as the #3264 / #3476 land detector. Close the unguarded filesystem route with a **new** check (pre-commit or a sibling verify) that a newly added `completed/` blob was written by `runTransition`, with the same historical-advisory / new-work-hard split doctor already uses for open items. Teach `scope:complete` to stamp a file already in `completed/` after merge so the leftover land PR is a stamp+commit, not a folder puzzle. Bind merge identity (#3675) before any stamp-quality gate. Until provenance is derived from the forge, treat the leftover chore as the designed land path — the thing #3476 refused to fold into the product PR — not as a hole this backstop forgot to close.

## Verdict

**Refuted.**

The target (“make completion provenance mandatory in the committed artifact and have `verify:completed-tracked` enforce it”) treats a land detector as a stamp-quality detector. Presence-only is not wrong. The defect is the unguarded route into `completed/` (here: `scope-provenance` stripped `active/`, then a hand-added `completed/` blob satisfied the land gate and skipped the leftover chore). Enforcing the stamp on this verb would red the historical corpus, fight non-code and `fail` completes, trap husks the verb cannot restamp, and — while #3675 is open — offer `--merge-commit origin/master` as the way back to green.

The gate is not broken. The route around the verb is.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-24T16:04:30Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol
role: critic

Worked at `origin/master` = `269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc`. Issue #3679 evidentiary ceiling honored: body + comment `5397797475` only; no later issue comment informs this critique. I also read the #3674 arc and repository sources at that SHA.

## Steelman of the position I reject

Putting delivery provenance in the completed xBRIEF gives one self-contained, Git-versioned record. It survives forge outages, supports offline inspection, travels with a repository migration, and makes tampering visible in ordinary commit history. It also keeps explicit facts that Git cannot infer (`deployed`, `uatVerified`, non-delivery disposition, verifier/session identity) beside the scope they qualify. Given 169 completed artifacts already carrying `completionProvenance`, making `verify:completed-tracked` reject the exceptional unstamped artifact looks like the smallest fail-closed repair. That is the strongest case for the target. It is still the wrong data boundary.

## Findings

### F1 — A mandatory delivered stamp in the artifact structurally requires a post-merge mutation (`blocks-the-design`)

The #3674 constraint is real. [`evaluateDeliveryGate`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L354-L501) requires a non-null `mergeCommit`, refreshes `origin/<deliveryBranch>`, and calls `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; failure returns `not_delivered`/`merged_to_integration`, not a delivered provenance record. The file was introduced by [`4dab160f`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/commit/4dab160f14d8cfd2dd3ef11fab2d27d47e91adf6) on 2026-08-02. The delivering PR's squash/merge commit does not exist before merge, much less occur in the refreshed remote ref.

Therefore no reformulation that still means “this artifact's own PR was delivered” can be both truthful and pre-merge-satisfiable. Allowing a predicted SHA, PR head SHA, or `assumeEvidenceValidated` would erase the distinction the ancestry gate exists to make. Requiring that post-merge fact inside a file on the delivery branch makes a second branch mutation (normally a PR) architectural, not incidental. This directly blocks treating #3678's cheaper lifecycle PRs as permanent infrastructure before this boundary is decided.

### F2 — `completionProvenance` conflates derivable delivery facts with non-derivable local assertions (`blocks-the-design`)

The actual schema has 14 fields: `repository`, `implementationCommit`, `prNumber`, `prBase`, `mergeCommit`, `deliveryBranch`, `deliveryCommit`, `verifiedAt`, `verifier`, `disposition`, `handoffState`, `deployed`, `uatVerified`, and optional `completedSessionId` ([interface](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L32-L60)). Real recent records show this is not merely theoretical: [#3651's artifact](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/xbrief/completed/2026-08-23-3651-featdesign-critique-parent-side-substantiation-for-evidence.xbrief.json#L251-L265) carries PR 3670 and merge `7f2639cc…`; [#3657](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/xbrief/completed/2026-08-23-3657-fixdesign-critique-variant-table-relax-panel-conjunction.xbrief.json#L224-L238) has the same shape; recent records also carry `completedSessionId`.

Field-by-field:

- Reliably derivable after merge from Git plus a forge PR port: `implementationCommit` (PR head), `prNumber`, `prBase`, and `mergeCommit`. `repository` and `deliveryBranch` come from local remote/policy, not from the stamp. A delivered `disposition`/`handoffState` can then be computed by ancestry.
- Derivable only with a changed meaning: current `deliveryCommit` is the remote tip observed at verification, not necessarily the merge commit. The exact historical tip at arbitrary local `verifiedAt` is not reconstructible from current forge state without an event/receipt.
- Not forge-derivable: local `verifiedAt`, `verifier`, `completedSessionId`; explicit non-delivery dispositions; and `deployed`/`uatVerified` (the source explicitly says never infer those from Git).

Making the whole object mandatory because some members are valuable duplicates forge facts while still failing to prove the local assertions. The design must split “delivery receipt” from “completion assertion.”

### F3 — Forge-only derivation is also insufficient; the dilemma is false (`blocks-the-design`)

A live GitHub query is not a durable provenance system. PR association can be absent for direct pushes, altered by history/import strategy, unavailable offline, or lost in a forge migration. `verifiedAt` and the observed delivery tip are point-in-time facts; querying later cannot recreate them. The provider-neutral direction is real, although not yet adopted: [ADR-002](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/docs/decisions/ADR-002-forge-provider-azure-adoption.md) explicitly describes extracting GitHub behind a `ForgeProvider` contract. Hard-coding “ask GitHub forever” would add migration debt.

But that does not imply the receipt belongs inside the xBRIEF. Normalize provider output into a provider-neutral, append-only delivery receipt keyed by `(repository identity, issue/scope id, artifact blob hash, PR/head identity)`. After merge, a reconciler records the actual merge SHA, delivery ref/tip, provider event time, and verifier version. A Git-native implementation can use a dedicated CAS-updated ref (for example a namespaced notes/ref ledger) so it travels with the repository without rewriting the delivery branch. A service-backed implementation can use the same receipt schema and export/import it. Either preserves post-merge truth without a human-opened lifecycle PR.

### F4 — The pre-merge artifact should carry intent, not claim delivery (`sharpens-framing`)

The worker can truthfully know and commit before merge: repository identity, scope/issue id, candidate PR number, PR base, head/implementation SHA, intended delivery branch, expected terminal disposition, and a state such as `pending_delivery`/`pr_open`. `verify:completed-tracked --tip HEAD` can require and bind that intent to the artifact and PR head before merge. It must not call it `delivered`.

On merge, a merge webhook, merge queue/CI job, or the existing `swarm:finalize-cohort`/post-merge closer runs the reconciler. The post-merge DONE check verifies both: (1) the intent-bearing completed artifact is on the delivery ref, and (2) a matching receipt proves ancestry. Under human-merge policy, no worker can satisfy a “future merge happened” gate pre-merge; the correct ownership change is to give that gate to the durable post-merge reconciler, not manufacture foreknowledge.

### F5 — The losses from unstamping are real but narrower than the proposal claims (`sharpens-framing`)

Offline auditability and migration replay are load-bearing enough to reject live-forge-only derivation. Tamper evidence is useful, but ordinary JSON in a later commit is only repository-history evidence, not an independent attestation; a dedicated Git ref/receipt can be equally hash-bound. Forge independence argues for a neutral receipt schema and adapter, not for coupling post-merge facts to a mutable scope document. The explicit-only facts (`deployed`, `uatVerified`, non-delivery disposition) should remain committed in the artifact because no reconciler can derive them.

### F6 — In-tree prior art supports separate records with different durability contracts (`footnote`)

Directive already chooses record homes by semantics: significant choices are standalone tracked records in [`xbrief/decisions/`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/xbrief/decisions/README.md); triage uses an append-only audit log with replay/reconciliation; and delivery attempts use durable project-local ledgers keyed by scope/target/workflow ([types](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/269a07e57861baea293b871cce9e6764dfd6c0bc/packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/types.ts#L91-L119)). None is itself the right delivery-receipt store—the attempt ledger is local and operational—but they refute the assumption that every lifecycle fact belongs inside the xBRIEF.

## Road not taken

I did not propose weakening ancestry, accepting a predicted merge SHA, or treating the PR head as the merge. I also did not choose live-forge derivation with no durable receipt. Finally, I did not repurpose the delivery-attempt or triage ledgers: their retention and trust boundaries do not meet repository-level delivery audit needs.

## Verdict

**Qualified.** The refutation target is **refuted** under its natural reading: post-merge delivery provenance (`mergeCommit`, observed delivery tip, delivered disposition) must not be mandatory inside the committed xBRIEF, because that makes a post-merge delivery-branch rewrite structurally necessary. It is **upheld only under a narrower reading**: the artifact must carry pre-merge completion intent plus explicit non-derivable assertions, and `verify:completed-tracked` should enforce that shape. Actual delivery provenance belongs in a provider-neutral, append-only receipt reconciled after merge and hash-bound to the committed artifact; the post-merge gate verifies artifact + receipt together.

Finding counts: `blocks-the-design` 3; `sharpens-framing` 2; `footnote` 1.

#3679 bound to two coupled defects: the unguarded write into `completed/`, and the absent recovery path with its dead #3041 branch. Both boundary-independent. `verify:completed-tracked` unchanged.

Split out: #3686 — delivery provenance belongs in a post-merge receipt rather than the committed artifact. That issue owns the fourteen-field split, the provider-neutral receipt, the post-merge reconciler, and the separate pre-merge intent check.

#3678 finishes as a transitional saving rather than permanent infrastructure. #3680 parks until #3686 decides whether the PR class it would optimize continues to exist.

## Note on the parent's contribution

I filed this issue, its parent, and three siblings, and disclosed that #3678 — building at the time — only has value if lifecycle PRs persist. My scope section operationalized only the option that preserves them. All three critics identified that independently, and the panel converged on the answer that makes my own in-flight work less necessary.

Three of my five markers are refuted. The corrected causal chain, the compliance measurement, and the dead-code finding are all things I did not have and would not have found alone.
